header.name: Biophysics
header.description: This biophysics course shall delve into concepts of physics acting upon biomolecules, primarily proteins. From understanding protein folding to predicting 3-dimension structures from the 1-dimension sequence, the course shall involve assignments that shall give the students the neccessary knowledge to deal with structural problems.
prerequisites_desirable: Basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, physics and python

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to understand the relation of protein evolution with its function and explain fundamental structural properties

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to decipher fundamentals forces acting upon biomolecules

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to extract meaningful Thermodynamic analysis and are able to explain the underlying connection with statistical physics for structure prediction

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to apply statistical and statistical-mechanical ideas to a solve complex biological systems.

lecture_topics: Introduction to Statistical Mechanics and basic mathematics in biophysics
Electrostatics and other interactions in proteins & water
Secondary structure and amino acid properties
Free energy and the hydrophobic effect

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment:  (1) where students will actually simulate protein/DNA or their interactions using computers.

lecture_topics: Thermodynamics of structural transitions, folding & denaturation
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment: (2) where students are going to simulate folding

lecture_topics: Insertion, Folding & Interactions of Membrane Proteins
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment:  (3) where students will actually predict protein structures using computers.
Assignment: (4) Structure prediction : From sequence to structure and analysis

lecture_topics: Secondary structure stability, helix-coil transitions & cooperativity
Statistical mechanics, the partition function, and first-order phase transitions

resources.title: Protein Physics A Course of Lectures by Alexei V. Finkelstein and Oleg B. Ptitsyn
Physical Biology of the Cell, Second Edition by Rob Phillips, Jane Kondev, Julie Theriot, and Hernan Garcia (Garland Science, 2012)
Introductory Biophysics by J. R. Claycomb and J.Q.P. Tran
